2.modern-en: The Exordium presents four imagined retellings of the Moriah story, each exploring a different way Abraham might have felt or acted — masking terror from Isaac, growing old and darkened after the return, riding in silence with grief — all concluding that no one was as great as Abraham, yet no one can understand him.
2.modern-da: Stemningen præsenterer fire forestillede genfortællinger af Morija-historien, der udforsker, hvordan Abraham måske handlede eller følte — skjuler rædsel for Isak, bliver gammel og formørket efter hjemkomsten, rider i stilhed med sorgen. Alle slutter med: ingen var stor som Abraham, og ingen kan forstå ham.

3.modern-en: The Eulogy celebrates Abraham as greater than all other heroes — not through worldly strength or wisdom, but through a faith that is weakness, folly, and madness to the world. Kierkegaard traces Abraham's decades of waiting for Isaac, his acceptance of God's command, and his absolute trust that God would provide — calling him great by a strength whose power is weakness.
3.modern-da: Lovtalen priser Abraham som større end alle andre helte — ikke ved verdslig styrke eller visdom, men ved en tro, der for verden er svaghed, dårskab og galskab. Kierkegaard skildrer Abrahams årtier med at vente på Isak, hans accept af Guds befaling og hans absolutte tillid til, at Gud ville sørge for det.

4.modern-en: Johannes de Silentio wrestles with Abraham's paradox: ethically, what Abraham intended was murder; religiously, it was sacrifice. The chapter insists that only the one who 'draws the knife receives Isaac' — that genuine faith is won through anguish, not by inheriting Abraham's name or paying lip-service to his deed.
4.modern-da: Johannes de Silentio kæmper med Abrahams paradoks: etisk set var det, Abraham ville, mord; religiøst set var det et offer. Kapitlet fastslår, at kun den, der 'drager kniven, modtager Isak' — at ægte tro vindes gennem angst, ikke ved at arve Abrahams navn eller hylde hans gerning med tomme ord.

5.modern-en: Problema I argues that Abraham teleologically suspended the ethical — placing his absolute duty to God above the universal moral law that forbids killing one's son. Unlike tragic heroes such as Agamemnon or Jephthah, Abraham acts for no universal cause; his deed is a purely private, paradoxical act of faith that cannot be mediated or explained.
5.modern-da: Problem I argumenterer for, at Abraham teleologisk suspenderede det etiske — at han satte sin absolutte pligt over for Gud over den universelle morallov, der forbyder at slå sin søn ihjel. I modsætning til tragiske helte som Agamemnon handler Abraham for ingen universel sag; hans gerning er en rent privat, paradoksal troshandling, der ikke kan formidles eller forklares.

6.modern-en: Problema II asks whether there is an absolute duty toward God that can override the ethical. Kierkegaard concludes that Abraham's silence and his willingness to sacrifice Isaac demonstrate precisely such a duty — one that cannot be expressed in universal terms without dissolving into a temptation and ceasing to be faith.
6.modern-da: Problem II spørger, om der findes en absolut pligt over for Gud, der kan tilsidesætte det etiske. Kierkegaard konkluderer, at Abrahams tavshed og hans vilje til at ofre Isak netop demonstrerer en sådan pligt — en pligt, der ikke kan udtrykkes i universelle vendinger uden at opløses til fristelse og ophøre med at være tro.

7.modern-en: Problema III examines why Abraham was silent — not speaking to Sarah, Eliezer, or Isaac before the journey. His silence is neither the aesthetically admirable silence of a tragic hero nor a failure of honesty; it is the necessary hiddenness of the single individual who stands in an absolute relation to the absolute, and who speaks a language no one else can hear.
7.modern-da: Problem III undersøger, hvorfor Abraham tavshed — han talte hverken med Sara, Elieser eller Isak inden rejsen. Hans tavshed er hverken den æstetisk beundringsverdige tavshed fra en tragisk helt eller en svigten over for ærlighed; det er den nødvendige skjulthed for det enkelte individ, der står i et absolut forhold til det absolutte, og som taler et sprog ingen anden kan høre.

8.modern-en: The Epilogue returns to Abraham as the measure of faith's highest passion: no generation inherits faith from the last, each must begin again from the beginning. Abraham's life is the permanent frontier — no one goes further than faith, and to claim otherwise is idle talk.
8.modern-da: Epilogen vender tilbage til Abraham som troens højeste lidenskabs målestok: ingen generation arver tro fra den forrige; hver må begynde forfra fra begyndelsen. Abrahams liv er den permanente grænse — ingen går videre end troen, og at påstå det modsatte er tom snak.

epithet.en: Son of the promise, would-be sacrifice

2.modern-en: In the four imagined variations, Isaac appears as the trusting child walking beside his father — sometimes terrified when Abraham turns wild-eyed, sometimes losing his faith when he glimpses his father's clenched fist. His vulnerability and innocence make each retelling more anguishing.
2.modern-da: I de fire forestillede variationer fremtræder Isak som det tillidsfulde barn ved siden af sin far — sommetider forskrækket, når Abraham ser vild ud, sommetimes mister han troen, da han ser faderens knyttede hånd. Hans sårbarhed og uskyld gør hver genfortælling mere pinende.

3.modern-en: The Eulogy identifies Isaac as the content of Abraham's entire life — his only beloved son, the child of the promise given after seventy years of waiting, which makes God's command to sacrifice him all the more incomprehensible and the act of faith all the more staggering.
3.modern-da: Lovtalen identificerer Isak som indholdet af hele Abrahams liv — hans eneste elskede søn, løftets barn givet efter halvfjerds års venten, hvilket gør Guds befaling om at ofre ham endnu mere ufattelig og troshandlingen endnu mere overvældende.

4.modern-en: Kierkegaard argues that what makes Abraham's trial so extreme is precisely his love for Isaac — a love so total that the command to sacrifice him is not an abstract test but the annihilation of Abraham's dearest joy. Only by drawing the knife — by fully intending to sacrifice Isaac — does faith reveal itself.
4.modern-da: Kierkegaard argumenterer for, at det, der gør Abrahams prøvelse så ekstrem, netop er hans kærlighed til Isak — en kærlighed så total, at befalingen om at ofre ham ikke er en abstrakt prøve, men udryddelsen af Abrahams kæreste glæde. Kun ved at drage kniven — ved fuldt ud at have til hensigt at ofre Isak — åbenbarer troen sig.

7.modern-en: The chapter focuses on why Abraham could not tell Isaac what was happening. Abraham's only preserved words — 'God will see to the lamb' — are analyzed as an act of irony that says everything and nothing: they neither lie nor reveal the paradox, because the paradox cannot be expressed in human language.
7.modern-da: Kapitlet fokuserer på, hvorfor Abraham ikke kunne fortælle Isak, hvad der foregik. Abrahams eneste bevarede ord — 'Gud vil se til et lam' — analyseres som en ironisk handling, der siger alt og intet: de lyver hverken eller afslører paradokset, fordi paradokset ikke kan udtrykkes på menneskeligt sprog.

2.modern-en: Sarah appears in the Exordium's retellings watching from the window as Abraham and Isaac ride away until they are no longer visible. In one variation she is kissed goodbye as 'the bride of his old age'; in another, her sorrow after the return is implied by Abraham's inability to forget what God demanded.
2.modern-da: Sara optræder i Stemningens genfortællinger og ser ud ad vinduet, da Abraham og Isak rider bort, indtil de ikke kan ses mere. I en variation kysses hun farvel som 'sin alderdoms brud'; i en anden antydes hendes sorg efter hjemkomsten af Abrahams manglende evne til at glemme, hvad Gud krævede.

3.modern-en: The Eulogy mentions Sarah as the one who 'laughed when the promise was first proclaimed' — her skepticism and eventual joy at Isaac's birth serve to measure the depth of Abraham's unshaken faith. When Isaac is born, Sarah stands 'as bride on the day of her golden wedding.'
3.modern-da: Lovtalen nævner Sara som den, der 'lo, da løftet først blev forkyndt' — hendes skepsis og endelige glæde ved Isaks fødsel er med til at måle dybden af Abrahams urokelige tro. Når Isak fødes, står Sara 'som brud på guldbryllupsdag.'

6.modern-en: Sarah is briefly noted as the one Abraham could not speak to before the journey to Moriah. Her exclusion from Abraham's silence is part of Kierkegaard's broader argument: the paradox of faith cannot be shared even with those one loves most.
6.modern-da: Sara nævnes kortvarigt som den, Abraham ikke kunne tale med inden rejsen til Morija. Hendes udelukkelse fra Abrahams tavshed er en del af Kierkegaards bredere argument: troens paradoks kan ikke deles selv med dem, man elsker mest.

7.modern-en: Problema III names Sarah first in the list of those Abraham was silent toward. She represents the ethical community — the one whose grief, understanding, or protest might have pulled Abraham back from the paradox, and to whom he therefore could say nothing.
7.modern-da: Problem III nævner Sara først på listen over dem, Abraham tav over for. Hun repræsenterer det etiske fællesskab — den, hvis sorg, forståelse eller protest måske ville have trukket Abraham tilbage fra paradokset, og til hvem han derfor intet kunne sige.

2.modern-en: In one of the Exordium's retellings, Eliezer accompanies Abraham along the road and turns back before the final ascent of Mount Moriah — the only witness to Abraham's departure who is named, yet the one most clearly left behind.
2.modern-da: I en af Stemningens genfortællinger ledsager Elieser Abraham ad vejen og vender tilbage inden den endelige bestigning af Morijabjerget — det eneste navngivne vidne til Abrahams afrejse, og den der tydeligst lades tilbage.

7.modern-en: Problema III names Eliezer alongside Sarah and Isaac as those Abraham chose not to tell. Like them, Eliezer represents the human world that would have offered counter-arguments, consolation, or protest — a world Abraham had to leave behind in silence in order to fulfill the paradox.
7.modern-da: Problem III nævner Elieser side om side med Sara og Isak som dem, Abraham valgte ikke at fortælle det. Som dem repræsenterer Elieser den menneskelige verden, der ville have tilbudt modargumenter, trøst eller protest — en verden, Abraham måtte forlade i tavshed for at opfylde paradokset.

1.modern-en: Johannes de Silentio introduces himself in the Preface as a freelance writer who is 'by no means a philosopher' and cannot understand the Hegelian System. He positions himself as a humble outsider who writes because it is a luxury — not to build systems, but to wrestle with what philosophy cannot grasp: faith.
1.modern-da: Johannes de Silentio introducerer sig selv i Forordet som en fri skribent, der 'på ingen måde er filosof' og ikke kan forstå det hegelianske system. Han positionerer sig selv som en ydmyg outsider, der skriver, fordi det er en luksus — ikke for at bygge systemer, men for at kæmpe med det, som filosofien ikke kan gribe: tro.

3.modern-en: In the Eulogy, Johannes functions as the poet who cannot do what the hero does but can only admire him. He confesses he cannot 'think himself into Abraham,' that every time he approaches the paradox he is thrown back and paralyzed — yet he refuses to dismiss faith as something lower than philosophy.
3.modern-da: I Lovtalen fungerer Johannes som digteren, der ikke kan gøre, hvad helten gør, men kun beundre ham. Han bekender, at han ikke kan 'tænke sig ind i Abraham,' at han hver gang han nærmer sig paradokset bliver kastet tilbage og lammet — og dog nægter han at afvise troen som noget lavere end filosofien.

4.modern-en: Johannes confesses that he lacks the courage to make the movement of faith and cannot make himself believe by virtue of the absurd. He distinguishes his own resigned, melancholy posture — 'married with the left hand' — from the full joy of faith, insisting that faith is the highest thing, not something philosophy can replace.
4.modern-da: Johannes bekender, at han mangler modet til at gøre troens bevægelse og ikke kan bringe sig selv til at tro i kraft af det absurde. Han skelner sin egen resignerende, melankolske holdning — 'gift med venstre hånd' — fra troens fulde glæde, og insisterer på, at troen er det højeste, ikke noget filosofien kan erstatte.

5.modern-en: Johannes works through the concept of the teleological suspension of the ethical, contrasting Abraham with tragic heroes like Agamemnon, Jephthah, and Brutus. He admits he can understand the tragic hero but cannot understand Abraham — and uses this admission as proof that Abraham is genuinely beyond philosophical comprehension.
5.modern-da: Johannes arbejder gennem begrebet om den teleologiske suspension af det etiske og sammenligner Abraham med tragiske helte som Agamemnon, Jefta og Brutus. Han indrømmer, at han kan forstå den tragiske helt, men ikke Abraham — og bruger denne indrømmelse som bevis for, at Abraham genuint ligger hinsides filosofisk forståelse.

6.modern-en: Johannes examines whether there is an absolute duty toward God, developing the concept of the knight of faith who stands in an absolute relation to the absolute. He describes his own inability to make this movement while insisting it is real and the highest — admiring the knight of faith as someone he could watch for hours without comprehending.
6.modern-da: Johannes undersøger, om der findes en absolut pligt over for Gud, og udvikler begrebet om troens ridder, der står i et absolut forhold til det absolutte. Han beskriver sin egen manglende evne til at gøre denne bevægelse, mens han insisterer på, at den er reel og den højeste — han beundrer troens ridder som en, han kunne betragte i timevis uden at forstå ham.

7.modern-en: Johannes concludes Problema III by tracing Abraham's silence as the only possible response to the paradox: he cannot speak because the paradox admits no universal expression. The lone preserved phrase — 'God will see to the lamb' — is analyzed as an ironic non-answer that honors both the impossibility of speech and the reality of faith.
7.modern-da: Johannes afslutter Problem III ved at spore Abrahams tavshed som det eneste mulige svar på paradokset: han kan ikke tale, fordi paradokset ikke tillader noget universelt udtryk. Den eneste bevarede sætning — 'Gud vil se til et lam' — analyseres som et ironisk ikke-svar, der ærer både talens umulighed og troens virkelighed.

8.modern-en: In the Epilogue, Johannes steps back to reflect on faith as the highest passion — one no generation inherits from the last. He affirms that he himself 'does not conceal that he has long prospects ahead of him' with respect to faith, and ends with a meditation on how it is enough to stop at faith, since no one comes further.
8.modern-da: I Epilogen træder Johannes et skridt tilbage og reflekterer over troen som den højeste lidenskab — en, som ingen generation arver fra den forrige. Han bekræfter, at han selv 'ikke skjuler, at han har lange udsigter foran sig' med hensyn til troen, og slutter med en betragtning over, at det er nok at stå ved troen, da ingen kommer videre.

epithet.en: Kierkegaard's ideal of the faithful individual
epithet.da: Kierkegaards ideal for det troende individ

4.modern-en: The concept of the knight of faith first emerges in contrast to the knight of infinite resignation. The knight of faith not only renounces the finite but — by virtue of the absurd — receives it back whole. Unlike the tragic hero who rests in the universal, the knight of faith makes a double movement: resignation and then faithful repossession.
4.modern-da: Begrebet om troens ridder opstår første gang i kontrast til den uendelige resignations ridder. Troens ridder ikke blot forsager det endelige, men — i kraft af det absurde — modtager det tilbage i sin helhed. I modsætning til den tragiske helt, der hviler i det universelle, gør troens ridder en dobbelt bevægelse: resignation og derefter troens genvinding.

5.modern-en: In Problema I, the knight of faith is distinguished sharply from the tragic hero. The tragic hero remains within the ethical; the knight of faith suspends the ethical by standing in an absolute relation to the absolute. Abraham is identified as the paradigmatic knight of faith — neither tragic hero nor murderer, but something the understanding cannot reach.
5.modern-da: I Problem I skelnes troens ridder skarpt fra den tragiske helt. Den tragiske helt forbliver inden for det etiske; troens ridder suspenderer det etiske ved at stå i et absolut forhold til det absolutte. Abraham identificeres som den paradigmatiske troens ridder — hverken tragisk helt eller morder, men noget forståelsen ikke kan nå.

6.modern-en: Problema II develops the knight of faith as the one who possesses an absolute duty toward God. Johannes offers an extended description: the knight looks like an ordinary bourgeois, enjoys a roasted lamb's head with vegetables, has no outward sign of the infinite — yet at every moment makes the movement of infinity and takes the finite back by virtue of the absurd.
6.modern-da: Problem II udvikler troens ridder som den, der har en absolut pligt over for Gud. Johannes giver en udvidet beskrivelse: ridderne ligner et almindeligt borgerskab, nyder et stegt lammehoved med grøntsager, har intet ydre tegn på det uendelige — og dog gør han til enhver tid uendelighedens bevægelse og tager det endelige tilbage i kraft af det absurde.

epithet.en: One who renounces the finite but cannot receive it back
epithet.da: Den der forsager det endelige, men ikke kan modtage det tilbage

4.modern-en: Infinite resignation is introduced as the last stage before faith — the movement in which the individual fully surrenders the beloved or the desired finite thing and gains in return eternal consciousness and spiritual peace. Johannes can make this movement himself but cannot take the further step of faith that would give back what was resigned.
4.modern-da: Uendelig resignation introduceres som det sidste trin før troen — den bevægelse, hvori individet fuldt ud opgiver den elskede eller det ønskede endelige og til gengæld vinder evig bevidsthed og åndelig fred. Johannes kan selv gøre denne bevægelse, men kan ikke tage det videre skridt af tro, der ville give det resignerede tilbage.

5.modern-en: In Problema I, the knight of infinite resignation is contrasted with the knight of faith: the former gives up Isaac and makes peace with the loss; the latter gives up Isaac and then — by virtue of the absurd — believes he will receive him back. The difference is not of degree but of kind: one stops at resignation, the other passes through it into faith.
5.modern-da: I Problem I stilles den uendelige resignations ridder i kontrast til troens ridder: den førstnævnte opgiver Isak og forligter sig med tabet; sidstnævnte opgiver Isak og tror derefter — i kraft af det absurde — at han vil modtage ham tilbage. Forskellen er ikke gradsmæssig men artsmæssig: den ene stopper ved resignationen, den anden passerer igennem den til troen.

epithet.en: Philosopher of the universal, Kierkegaard's foil

1.modern-en: The Preface opens by mocking the age's presumption of having mastered doubt and gone 'beyond' faith — an implicit critique of the Hegelian claim that philosophy has superseded all earlier stages of spirit. Johannes positions himself against this ambition from the start.
1.modern-da: Forordet åbner med at spotte tidens formodning om at have mestret tvivlen og at have bevæget sig 'videre' end troen — en implicit kritik af den hegelianske påstand om, at filosofien har overgået alle tidligere åndens stadier. Johannes positionerer sig imod denne ambition fra begyndelsen.

5.modern-en: Problema I directly engages Hegel: Kierkegaard argues that Hegel is right that the individual must express himself in the universal — but wrong to speak of faith while praising Abraham. If Hegel's ethics is the highest, then Abraham is a murderer, not a hero of faith. Kierkegaard uses Hegel as the limit-case against which Abraham's paradox becomes fully visible.
5.modern-da: Problem I indgår direkte med Hegel: Kierkegaard argumenterer for, at Hegel har ret i, at individet må udtrykke sig i det universelle — men forkert i at tale om tro, mens han roser Abraham. Hvis Hegels etik er det højeste, er Abraham en morder, ikke en troens helt. Kierkegaard bruger Hegel som grænsetilfælde, over for hvilket Abrahams paradoks bliver fuldt synligt.

6.modern-en: Problema II returns to the Hegelian system: Hegel holds that the outer is higher than the inner, so every person must express their inwardness outwardly through the ethical. Kierkegaard argues that faith is precisely the paradox that inverts this — inwardness is higher than outwardness — and that Hegel's philosophy cannot accommodate faith without destroying it.
6.modern-da: Problem II vender tilbage til det hegelianske system: Hegel mener, at det ydre er højere end det indre, så enhver person må udtrykke sin inderlighed udadtil gennem det etiske. Kierkegaard argumenterer for, at troen netop er det paradoks, der vender dette om — inderlighed er højere end uderlighed — og at Hegels filosofi ikke kan rumme troen uden at ødelægge den.

4.modern-en: In the Preliminary Expectoration, Hegel's philosophy is caricatured as theology dressed like a courtesan, selling its charms to philosophy. Kierkegaard's Johannes says he has studied Hegel diligently and understood him — but when he tries to think about Abraham he is 'annihilated,' whereas Hegel seems to handle everything easily. This contrast is the book's central provocation.
4.modern-da: I den foreløbige Expectoration karikeres Hegels filosofi som teologi klædt som en kurtisane, der sælger sine charme til filosofien. Kierkegaards Johannes siger, at han har studeret Hegel flittigt og forstået ham — men når han forsøger at tænke på Abraham, bliver han 'tilintetgjort', hvorimod Hegel synes at håndtere alt med lethed. Denne kontrast er bogens centrale provokation.
